discovery: Discovery of topological insulators and their quantized edge transport: the quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall effects

nominees.name: Qi-Kun Xue
nominees.affiliation: Southern University of Science and Technology and Tsinghua University, China

motivation: Topological insulators revealed that band topology protected by symmetry, not only magnetic fields, can produce quantized, dissipationless transport. Charles Kane, with Eugene Mele, introduced the Z2 invariant and predicted the quantum spin Hall state, turning Berry-phase ideas into a classification of ordinary crystalline insulators. Laurens Molenkamp first observed the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe quantum wells in 2007, confirming quantized helical edge conduction. Qi-Kun Xue, through heroic molecular-beam-epitaxy control of magnetically doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3 films, observed in 2013 the quantum anomalous Hall effect: quantized Hall resistance at zero magnetic field, a state predicted by first-principles theory. Together these works exemplify the full chain from concept to materials prediction to decisive experiment. They launched the field of topological materials, now encompassing Dirac and Weyl semimetals, axion insulators and topological superconductors, and underpin prospects for low-dissipation electronics and topological quantum computation.
